data.name: Monitor_Name
data.value: Adaptive Agent for PHD2 — Sky Conditions

data.name: Monitor_Description
data.value:
Continuously measures observing conditions and reports them to N.I.N.A. as a safety device. (It appears under the “Safety Monitor” category: that is N.I.N.A.'s name for the slot, not this monitor's role.)
Since version 1.14 the guide camera judges the sky, in both directions: the guide star sits in the same telescope as the imaging camera and is measured every few seconds, even while the sequence is paused. It needs Adaptive Agent 3.1 or later: with an older Agent the imaging camera judges the sky, as in 1.13.
It reports UNSAFE on: a star lost for a long time; a guide-star signal below half of its clear-sky level (after about 3.5 minutes with the factory settings: clouds, or a guide-camera fault); a guide channel gone silent while guiding was expected; the Agent unreachable during an active session. It returns SAFE when the guide star stays above 80% of its clear-sky level for a minute and is tracked steadily: about 2 minutes after the sky clears. During calibration, the Guiding Assistant and autofocus (when N.I.N.A. stops guiding for it) the sky verdict is suspended; a lost star, however, still counts. The imaging camera measures the sky on every frame but is informational only.
ADVANCED SEQUENCER — recommended setup: Trigger On Unsafe └ Before Waiting For Safety └ Recovery probe (Adaptive Agent)
With the guide channel as judge the instruction takes no exposures: it keeps guiding alive. If guiding stops while waiting, if the star stays lost for long, or if unsafe lasts beyond the safety cadence, it restarts guiding; it ends on its own when the monitor returns SAFE. Do not put instructions that stop guiding or park (Park, Find Home, Stop Guiding) in the unsafe branch.
The monitor only reports: N.I.N.A.'s Sequence Engine stays in charge of the sequence, your end-of-sequence criteria always win, and any running recovery is cancelled the moment the sequence ends.

data.name: Probe_AutoTimeout
data.value: Auto cadence

data.name: Probe_AutoTimeout_Tip
data.value: Only with the imaging camera as judge. Recommended. The probe cadence is derived from the Agent's telemetry freshness window minus the probe exposure, so sky data never goes stale between probes — and it never waits more than 3 minutes (field-validated) when the window would allow a faster check. It adapts by itself to your sub length. Uncheck to force a fixed timeout in minutes.

data.name: Probe_FallbackExp
data.value: Fallback exposure (s)

data.name: Probe_FallbackExp_Tip
data.value: Only with the imaging camera as judge. Used ONLY if no LIGHT has been saved yet this session (for example right after restarting N.I.N.A.). In every other case the probe replicates the interrupted sub exactly — required by the transparency index, whose star-count comparison is not normalized for exposure time.

data.name: Probe_MinInterval_Tip
data.value: Minimum interval between two probe actions. With the guide channel as judge: between two guiding restarts, and also how long guiding must have stopped, or the star been lost, before it is restarted. With the camera as judge: between two probe exposures, guide-SNR hint included.

data.name: Probe_Timeout_Tip
data.value: Safety cadence. With the guide channel as judge: after how many minutes of continued unsafe, with guiding running, the probe restarts the guide channel (on 3/10 a guide-camera fault cleared exactly at a guiding restart). With the camera as judge: how long it waits before a verification exposure when the guide-SNR hint has not fired earlier; there it is used only while “Auto cadence” is off.

data.name: Settings_GuideObs_Check
data.value: Report unsafe when the guide channel goes silent

data.name: Settings_GuideObs_Help
data.value: Watches whether PHD2 is still delivering guide frames at all — not how good the guiding is (that is the engine's job). Legitimate pauses (meridian flip, autofocus, manual stop) are announced by PHD2 and never raise an alarm; a guide camera that dies stops talking instead, and that silence is what this detects. A severe PHD2 alert or a burst of per-frame star errors halves the delay.

data.value: Sky Conditions — guide channel observability

data.name: Settings_GuidePolls
data.value: Silent → unsafe (polls):

data.name: Settings_GuidePolls_Tip
data.value: Polls of confirmed silence before declaring UNSAFE. Frames flowing again drain the count. Higher = more tolerant of brief gaps.

data.name: Settings_GuideSilence
data.value: Silence threshold (s):

data.name: Settings_GuideSilence_Tip
data.value: Seconds without ANY guide frame (guiding or re-acquisition attempts) before the channel is considered suspect. Halved when corroborated by a severe PHD2 alert or repeated per-frame star errors.

data.name: Settings_Meridian_Label
data.value: Sky Conditions — meridian protection

data.name: Settings_Meridian_Check
data.value: Authorize the mechanical meridian flip during a long unsafe hold

data.name: Settings_Meridian_Help
data.value: Without this, NINA reacts to an unsafe flip deadline by stopping mount tracking — and nothing ever restarts it: the guide star drifts away, frames trail, and the monitor loses every eye it decides with. The night ends there even if the sky clears (verified on 19/7). This window briefly reports safe so the flip alone can run, then immediately restores the unsafe hold: it protects the monitor's own ability to keep observing, it never judges the sky. Reconsider only if other devices (roof, dome) start consuming this monitor's safe state.

data.name: Settings_MeridianLead
data.value: Open window (min before flip deadline):

data.name: Settings_MeridianLead_Tip
data.value: How many minutes before the flip deadline (meridian + your NINA 'max minutes after meridian') the window opens. Arriving early lets the flip run through NINA's normal path before the tracking-stop guard fires.

data.name: Settings_ProbeGate_Check
data.value: Defer recovery probes while the guide channel is unstable

data.name: Settings_ProbeGate_Help
data.value: Only with the imaging camera as judge: with the guide channel as judge the Recovery probe takes no exposures. A 300 s probe deserves a stable guide channel: while the channel is declared not ready the timed probe slides — never beyond a hard 15-minute ceiling.

data.name: Settings_SkyDegrade_Check
data.value: With the imaging camera as judge: report unsafe sooner when the guide star fades

data.name: Settings_SkyDegrade_Polls
data.value: Guide-star fade → unsafe (polls):

data.name: Settings_Tip_SkyDegradePolls
data.value: How long the guide-star signal must stay collapsed before UNSAFE, after the 90 s the Agent needs to confirm it. With the factory settings: 8 polls × 15 s = 2 minutes, about 3.5 minutes in total. With the imaging camera as judge it is separate from the camera threshold ("Degraded → unsafe"): raising one never slows the other.

data.name: Settings_SkyDegrade_Help
data.value: Only with the imaging camera as judge: the guide star is sampled every few seconds and a collapse of its signal counts toward unsafe straight away, before the next frame. With the guide channel as judge the guide-star collapse is the cloud path and always counts: this box does not turn it off.

data.name: Settings_Index_Check
data.value: Use transparency index persistence (recommended)

data.name: Settings_Index_Help
data.value: Only with the imaging camera as judge. Accumulates degradation while the transparency index is low and drains it while the sky is clear; brief HAZE bounces no longer reset the cloud timer. Unchecked = legacy logic (consecutive CLOUD polls on the discrete state).

data.name: Settings_ManageExt_Check
data.value: Also manage an Agent not started by the plugin

data.name: Settings_ManageExt_Help
data.value: On (default): when NINA closes, the plugin gracefully shuts down any reachable Agent — even one it did not start — so the PHD2 baseline is always restored. Turn it off if you run the Agent standalone and want it to outlive NINA. Note: for an external Agent there is no process handle — if it hangs, only the Agent's own orphan recovery cleans up at next start.

data.name: Settings_Recovery_Body
data.value: That single instruction is the complete recovery loop. With the guide channel as judge (recommended) it takes no exposures: it waits for SAFE, which comes when the guide star confirms a clear sky, and if guiding stops or the star stays lost meanwhile it restarts guiding. Do not put instructions that stop guiding or park (Park, Find Home, Stop Guiding) in the unsafe branch: they would blind the only judge. Only with the option "The imaging camera can also report unsafe" does the instruction take verification exposures at the configured cadence again. No extra containers or Camera instructions are needed.

data.name: Settings_Recovery_Intro
data.value: To let the session resume by itself after clouds, add ONE instruction to your Advanced Sequence:

data.name: Settings_Recovery_Title
data.value: Automatic recovery — sequence setup

data.value: Stale → unsafe (polls):

data.name: Settings_Stale_Check
data.value: Report unsafe on stale telemetry under a degraded sky

data.name: Settings_Stale_Help
data.value: Only with the imaging camera as judge. If NINA telemetry stops arriving (beyond the adaptive freshness window — the normal gap between exposures does NOT trigger this) while the session is active and the last known sky was degraded, the monitor escalates to unsafe.

data.name: Settings_StarLost_Help
data.value: How long STAR_LOST must persist before the monitor reports unsafe. Default 5 minutes (300). Allowed range: 30–1800. Higher values reduce false positives at the cost of slower detection; lower values risk triggering on transient STAR_LOST events the Agent would have recovered.

data.name: Settings_StarLost_Label
data.value: Sky Conditions — STAR_LOST consolidation (seconds)

data.name: Settings_Telemetry_Check
data.value: Telemetry forwarding enabled

data.name: Settings_Telemetry_Help
data.value: On every saved exposure, sends HFR, star count and image statistics to the Agent (HTTP POST). Optional: if the Agent is offline nothing happens and NINA is never disturbed. Disable to send no data.

data.name: Settings_Telemetry_Label
data.value: Forward NINA per-exposure metrics to the Agent

data.name: Settings_Tip_AccumBelow
data.value: Only with the imaging camera as judge. While the transparency index (0–1) is below this value, degradation accumulates. Higher = more sensitive to veils. Default matches the Agent's CLOUD threshold (0.5).

data.name: Settings_Tip_AgentLostPolls
data.value: Polls with the Agent unreachable before declaring UNSAFE. Escalates only during an active session — with guiding intentionally stopped, an offline Agent raises no alarm.

data.name: Settings_Tip_ClearPolls
data.value: Polls of clear sky, as seen by the active judge, needed to fully drain a saturated accumulator and clear the cloud UNSAFE. With the guide channel as judge, clear sky only counts while the star is tracked steadily. Higher = slower, more cautious return to safe.

data.name: Settings_Tip_DegradedPolls
data.value: Only with the imaging camera as judge (option "The imaging camera can also report unsafe"). Accumulated polls of degraded sky before declaring UNSAFE: clear sky drains the count, HAZE is neutral (no reset). Higher = more tolerant of brief veils. 1 poll = the polling interval (default 15 s).

data.name: Settings_Tip_DrainAbove
data.value: Only with the imaging camera as judge. While the index is at or above this value, accumulated degradation drains; between the two thresholds (HAZE) nothing changes. Lower = faster recovery to safe.

data.name: Settings_Tip_StalePolls
data.value: Only with the imaging camera as judge. Polls with stale telemetry (beyond the adaptive freshness window — the normal gap between exposures never counts) before UNSAFE. Escalates only with cloud safety on, an active session and the last known sky degraded.
